observation.visible_scene: A night-sky fireworks display captured over a short excerpt. The frame is dominated by a dark background punctuated by many small glowing sparks and star-like bursts, drifting clouds of red and white smoke, vertical fountain-like trails of gold/red sparks rising from the lower portion, and occasional large radial spark bursts. The display is already in progress at the first frame and still active at the last.
visible_changes: Multiple small bursts and scattered sparks appear, brighten, and fade across the upper and side regions throughout the segment.
A red smoke cloud in the lower-center grows and persists, becoming the dominant mid-frame feature from about t=1.1s onward.
Bright white/blue smoke clouds expand outward from burst centers (notably around t=0.13s, t=1.27s, t=1.53-1.6s, and t=2.4s), sometimes filling much of the frame with a bright flash.
Vertical fountain trails of gold and red sparks rise from the bottom edge (clear from ~t=0.9s onward), maintaining roughly the same horizontal positions while emitting sparks.
Radial spark bursts (gold/white streaks) expand outward from central points over the red smoke, e.g. around t=1.4-1.7s and t=2.0-2.3s.
The large white flash at t=1.8-1.9s and t=2.4s briefly washes out the scene before the red smoke and sparks re-emerge.
outside_clip_unknowns: The beginning and end of the overall fireworks show; bursts are mid-cycle at both crop boundaries.
The launch sources or shells that produced the bursts and fountains.
Whether the bright white flashes are single large detonations or overlapping bursts.
Events before t=0 and after the last frame.
uncertain_details: Camera motion: the background is a featureless dark sky, so any pan/tilt/zoom is not reliably distinguishable from the evolving fireworks; the framing appears mostly static.
Exact correspondence of individual sparks between frames due to low light and overlapping smoke.
Whether some bright points are reflections/lens flare or separate physical sparks.
